sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-impermeable HaloTag live labeling confirmed surface display of the extracellular HaloTag on HEK293T cells expressing the HaloTag-FLAG-ADGRL2 construct; no further functional assay of the receptor reported in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: The paper (L7/L8) states HaloTag-FLAG is placed 'immediately upstream of the native TA sequence' in full-length ADGRL2. The GPS cleavage motif HLT is located at residues 823–825 (Python search confirmed H=823, L=824, T=825); GPS cleavage releases the NTF and exposes the TA starting at residue 826 (N). Therefore the HaloTag C-terminus connects to residue 826, placing the junction at insert_after_residue=825 (T→N). This position is within the extracellular domain (26–851) and 26 residues from TM1 (852), satisfying the ≥3-residue constraint. The large HaloTag (~33 kDa) is tolerated at this junction, supporting that a short epitope tag (~15–23 aa) would also be accommodated. Full-length ADGRL2 construct in which the entire NTF was replaced by HaloTag-FLAG placed immediately upstream of the native tethered agonist (TA) sequence, expressed in HEK293T cells. Surface display of the extracellular HaloTag was confirmed by cell-impermeable HaloTag live labeling.

sources.claim: We initially confirmed the expression of the six fusion proteins with a cell-impermeable HaloTag live labeling protocol in HEK293T cells ( Fig. 1B ).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Both the HA-tagged extracellular moiety and the GFP-tagged intracellular moiety of HA-Lphn2-EGFP colocalized with vinculin at cell-to-ECM adhesion sites in cultured endothelial cells, matching the pattern of endogenous LPHN2; surface display of the N-terminal HA tag on the intact membrane-anchored protein confirmed.
sites.rationale: ADGRL2 has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–25 (computed landmark); the mature N-terminus begins at residue 26 (F). An N-terminal tag must be placed after SP cleavage, i.e., insert_after_residue=25, giving the junction G(25)|F(26). Python lookup confirms seq[25]=G and seq[26]=F. The paper (L4/L5/L6) reports HA-Lphn2-EGFP with the HA tag on the extracellular face, confirmed by colocalization with vinculin at ECM adhesions; L3 independently reports an N-terminal FLAG tag detected on the cell surface of Lphn2-expressing cells. Both papers name no specific residue, but the N-terminus after SP cleavage is the only extracellular terminus available for an N-terminal tag. Full-length mouse Lphn2 expressed with an N-terminal HA tag and C-terminal EGFP (HA-Lphn2-EGFP) in cultured endothelial cells; the N-terminal HA tag is extracellular and the C-terminal EGFP is intracellular. The same N-terminal extracellular junction is independently corroborated by an N-terminal FLAG tag on Lphn2 (L3) confirmed on the cell surface.

sources.claim: We found that, similarly to endogenous LPHN2, both the HA-tagged extracellular and the GFP-tagged intracellular moieties of HA-Lphn2-EGFP colocalized with vinculin at cell-to-ECM adhesion sites ( Fig. 1 B ).

literature_notes: Three ledger lines (L3, L4, L5/L6) all pin the same N-terminal extracellular junction (after SP cleavage at residue 25); they are treated as one site with L5 as the primary evidence (highest validation level: surface_and_function). L7/L8 pins a distinct internal junction at the GPS cleavage site (825/826) where the HaloTag C-terminus connects to the tethered agonist sequence; this is reported as a separate internal site. L1/L2 report an mVenus insertion at mouse Lphn2 position 1311/1312 (intracellular in human ADGRL2, topology 1084–1459) and are placed in other_positions. No ledger line supports any insertion in the short extracellular loops of the 7TM bundle (ECL1: 902–909, ECL2: 973–990, ECL3: 1057–1062).

literature_other_positions.note: mVenus inserted between mouse Lphn2 L1311 and T1312 in a full-length knock-in construct; human ADGRL2 residue 1311 (S) falls within the intracellular domain (1084–1459) and the mouse numbering does not map to an LT motif in the human sequence near this position.
